activity_context.topic_title: Properties of Definite Integrals Involving the Limits of Integration

feedback.worked_solution:
Let's reverse the limits of integration on the known result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{6}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{\int }_{6}^{1}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=7\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can split up the given integral using the sum rule and factor out the constants. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{6}(2f(x)-1)\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{1}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,-\,{\int }_{1}^{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2(7)\,-\,x\,{|}_{1}^{6} \\  & =14\,-\,(6-1) \\  & =14\,-\,5 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$
